Main charitable entity types: Nonprofit corporation (public-benefit, mutual-benefit or religious subtype) under the Corporations Act 2021 (RPPL 10-11, codified 12 PNCA Ch. 1), registered online with the Registrar of Corporations at the Financial Institutions Commission (FIC); corporations sole under separate ecclesiastical legislation.
Key local requirements: At least 1 director must be a lawful resident of Palau (1 director minimum; 1 incorporator suffices); registered agent and registered office in Palau named in the Articles; directors upload passport/ID scans with name, residential address and nationality; beneficial-ownership info kept for the Registrar; English; no notarisation or presidential signature any more
Est. cost & time: Government fee USD 150 (Articles, nonprofit) plus resident-director/registered-agent arrangements (private quotes, unpublished) and optional legal fees, roughly USD 500-2,000 in year one; Registrar issues the certificate in 1-2 business days once the online account is approved, but finding a trustworthy Palau-resident director typically takes weeks.
Notes: RPPL 10-11 (signed 29 Sep 2021) repealed the old 12 PNC corporations law; online register live 20 Jan 2025 and registrar role moved from the Office of the Attorney General to the FIC (Executive Order No. 477) | old 3-incorporator, notarised, President-signed procedure abolished | public-benefit nonprofits must pass assets to another public-benefit nonprofit on dissolution | entities not re-registered by Jan 2026 were administratively dissolved | Foreign Investment Act (28 PNCA Ch. 1, as amended by RPPL 9-64) targets foreign-owned 'business enterprises' needing an FIB certificate; a nonprofit barred from business activity normally needs none, but the Corporations Act does not displace the FIA and the 2019 border-security EO subjects foreign nonprofit founders to background checks | front-company crackdown: false filings to the Registrar are a crime
Main bottleneck (remote foreign founder): The Corporations Act requires at least one director who is a lawful resident of Palau, so an Australian founder must recruit a trusted local resident director (and registered agent) before the online filing can be lodged.
Registration fee (USD): ~$150 (USD 150 Articles of Incorporation, Palau nonprofit, code A-2; foreign nonprofit registration USD 500)
Charitable deduction regime: 40 PNC § 1104 historically refunds/credits donations to Palau non-profit corporations up to 10% of the taxpayer's wages or gross revenue; survival and mechanics after the 2023 tax reform (RPPL 11-11: PGST + Business Profits Tax) are unconfirmed; check with the Bureau of Revenue and Taxation.
Foreign donor / donation restrictions: None notable; no foreign-funding register, though FIC AML/CFT rules (Money Laundering Act, 17 PNCA Ch. 33) and beneficial-ownership disclosure apply and nonprofits may not engage in business.
Annual compliance & reporting: Online annual report to the FIC Registrar (USD 100 for a Palau nonprofit, USD 200 if late); file changes of directors, officers or addresses (USD 15, USD 100 late); maintain beneficial-ownership records available to the Registrar on request; no public accounts filing or statutory audit; non-filing removes good standing and leads to administrative dissolution (reinstatement possible).
Tax-exempt status & benefits: Automatic in practice: Business Profits Tax rules list the income of a resident nonprofit corporation as exempt income (12% BPT otherwise); PGST (10%) registration only above USD 300,000 taxable supplies or for FIB certificate holders; no separate charity-status application found.
Bank account (remote feasibility): Needs a local visit: the three FDIC-insured US bank branches (Bank of Hawaii, Bank of Guam, BankPacific) hold ~98% of deposits and open accounts on paper with in-person KYC in Koror, requiring certified Articles, bylaws, a director list and signatories' IDs; non-resident signatories face enhanced due diligence, so the resident director usually has to be a signatory.
